claims.gist: By 2025, 40% of boards will have cyber committees, from under 10%
Organizational changes respond to pandemic-expanded digital footprint
Boards rate cybersecurity second-highest enterprise risk
Few directors feel their company is properly secured
Many boards are forming confidential cybersecurity committees
Committee governance likely changes the board-CISO relationship
CISOs will get more scrutiny but also more support
CISO executive conversations should shift toward risk and value
By 2024, 60% of CISOs will partner with sales, finance, marketing
Effective CISOs treat business unit heads as key partners
Top CISOs meet three times more non-IT than IT stakeholders
Cyber-physical threats increasingly risk asset-intensive enterprises
Attackers increasingly target weaknesses, including ransomware and supply chains
Siloed security disciplines are a liability
Security teams must expand to physical-world threats
By 2025, 50% of asset-intensive organizations will converge security under a CSO
61% of organizations struggled to hire security professionals
Pandemic proved security capabilities can be delivered remotely
Cybersecurity teams can work remotely and remain effective
By 2022, 30% of security teams will increase permanent remote staff
Leaders should recruit outside traditional geographies

thesis: Expanded pandemic-era risk will drive board cyber committees, CISO business partnerships, converged security and remote security teams.
